tasks.instructions:
Experiment E1 (tests H39): Phase A as an asynchronous chain: all conv plane copies issued at entry, W1 converted while they land, W2 conversion and output prefill deferred into GEMM1 slack (tc_kernel and sc_kernel). STEP 0 (control and stamps, ~5 B200 min). Build the parent unchanged; run_tests once as the same-container control. Add TC_STAMPS globaltimer stamps taken by the warp that does the work (not tid 0 after a barrier): kernel start, W1 conversion end, W2 conversion end, out-prefill end, each conv unit's copy-issue / copy-landed / compute-end, sync 1 release, last GEMM1 tile end, sync 2 release, kernel end. Rows: 2,768 / 8,768 / 32,768 / 16,384 / 1,192 / 8,192. Check STACK in cuobjdump for the stamped build (r8: stamps alone pushed the 512-thread epilogue over 128 regs). Record the phase A breakdown per row; this is the baseline for the success criterion.
STEP 1 (conv copies at entry). At kernel entry each CTA issues the 1-D cp.async.bulk plane copies for ALL of its conv units (2-3 units per CTA at 16,384 / 32,768; check the per-row unit table) into distinct smem slots with one mbarrier per unit, before touching any weight. Phase A owns the whole 227 KB (the GEMM rings are unused until sync 1), so budget slots = units_per_cta x padded plane-group bytes and assert it per instantiation. Then convert the CTA's W1 share (fp16(lnw*W1) plus the u/c1 row sums, as now) on all warps, then wait each unit's barrier in order and run the conv + LN register stats + d16 stores exactly as now. Stamp again: the conv compute should start right after the W1 conversion with no landing wait.
STEP 2 (defer W2 and the prefill). Move the W2 -> fp16 conversion, b2' = W2.gb + b2 and the out = x + b2' prefill out of phase A into the GEMM1 phase. Static assignment per row: slices go first to CTAs with no GEMM1 tile (2,768: 124 idle of 148; 8,768: 52; the sc rows similarly), the remainder to CTAs after their last GEMM1 tile; every CTA finishes its deferred work before arriving at sync 2. Nothing in GEMM1 reads W2 or out; verify that GEMM2's first TMA of W2 and the red.add into out happen only after sync 2 (they do in the parent, keep it so). Keep the W2 pass as JB-wide float4 register loads before any shuffle (H r8 lesson) and avoid runtime-trip-count loops.
STEP 3 (stretch, only if STEP 1-2 are green with >= 60 B200 min of wall time left). Replace the two grid barriers by the flat self-resetting atomic-counter barrier from the r4 B microbench (one counter line per barrier, generation number, last arriver flips the flag, no __nanosleep: plain ld.acquire spin). Measure the release with the stamps (target <= 1.1 us vs the current 1.5-2). Keep it only if interleaved x3 shows >= 1 us per row.
STEP 4 (measure and ship). Interleave parent vs candidate x3 in one container with harness_time on all 13 D rows (6 tc + 7 sc). run_tests 16/16 including the portal-order re-runs. Precision: the roundings and summation orders are unchanged if STEP 1-3 only reorder work; state that explicitly and run a single-seed fp64 check per row; if any summation order changed (e.g. the b2' GEMV), redo the 10-seeded-round log for the affected paths. Record phase A per row before/after, the per-row interleaved deltas, and the smem budget per instantiation in the findings. Report which rows the merge should take. Success: Phase A stamps (kernel start to the last conv unit's compute end) <= 5.0 us at 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 and <= 3.5 us at 1,192, and interleaved x3 rows: 8,768 <= 30.5, 2,768 <= 23.5, 16,768 <= 41, 32,768 <= 61, 8,384 <= 31.5, 16,384 <= 49 us rented, with the sc rows >= 1.5 us faster than the parent; 16/16 pass; no new rounding. Refuted if: After STEP 1-2 the phase A stamps drop by < 1.5 us at 8,768 and 32,768, or the interleaved x3 rows are within 1 us of the parent on 4 or more of the 6 tc rows (then phase A is bound by something other than the serial chain: report the stamp that did not move). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) every red.add / atomic target (gsq per (image,k), split-K output) is still zeroed or prefilled inside the launch before the grid sync that precedes its first add; with the prefill moved into GEMM1 slack, out = x + b2' must be complete on every CTA before sync 2, as the plan says. Any grid-barrier counter, generation word or flag must live in a module-level __device__ buffer (zero-initialised at module load) and be self-reset by the last arriver, never in the torch.empty workspace (uninitialised, not guaranteed to be the same memory or unchanged between calls). Spin with plain ld.acquire loops, no __nanosleep. (z) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (TC_STAMPS/SC_STAMPS 0; the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. TMA descriptors encoded on every call. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes and plans set to one maximal value.

Experiment E2 (tests H33): GEMM2 as cta_group::2 pairs with a 6-stage half-tile ring in which g is produced by look-ahead warps, removing g from the GEMM1 epilogue (tc_kernel). STEP 0 (control and stamps, ~5 B200 min). Build the parent; run_tests once as the same-container control. Stamp GEMM2 per unit from the MMA warp and the drain warps: unit start, first stage landed, per-stage MMA issue (clock64 deltas, report clk per stage against the two-MMA ideal 2 x 2N clk per 64-k stage), mainloop end, drain end, red.add end; rows 8,768 / 32,768 / 16,384 / 2,768. Check STACK on the stamped build.
STEP 1 (pairs). Launch the cooperative kernel with cluster dims 2x1 (cudaLaunchKernelEx with both the cooperative and the cluster-dimension attributes; if the driver rejects the combination, fall back to a plain launch with grid <= residency checked per shape via cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters, and the flat self-resetting counter barrier for the two syncs, as F/H did). GEMM2 in the pair form from the lineage's validated recipe: M = 256 output channels across the pair (C=768: 3 pair M-tiles; C=384: one full pair tile plus one with 128 valid rows, A OOB zero-filled, epilogue masked, or keep the 1SM path for the 14x14 rows if the waste shows in the stamps), each CTA TMAs its own 128 A rows (W2, 16 KB per 64-k) and HALF of the B token tile (h 8 KB + g 8 KB) to the leader's full barrier via mapa, leader-only expect_tx of both CTAs' bytes, idesc M = 256>>4, tcgen05.commit .cta_group::2 .multicast::cluster mask 3, each CTA drains its own 128 TMEM lanes. Stage = 32 KB per CTA, ring depth 6. Retune KS per row so pair-units >= 74 x 1-2 (fewer, larger units than the 1SM version: 2 units per CTA at 32,768 today) and keep the coalesced red.add.v4 into the prefilled out. Validate vs torch on all six tc rows before timing. Stamp: clk per stage vs ideal and the GEMM2 phase per row.
STEP 2 (g out of GEMM1). GEMM1 epilogue writes h16 only and gw*gf per (image,k) into a [B][4C] fp32 array (the r8 smem-g variant did this: GEMM1 post -56 %). In GEMM2, 4 producer warps (not the drain warps, not the MMA warp) wait each stage's full barrier, build g16 = fp16(c[k] * h16) for the CTA's half tile (8 KB: 32 lanes x 4 warps x 64 B) into the stage's g buffer with c[k] = gw[k]*gf[img(token)][k] loaded once per unit into smem (one image group per N tile; at 7x7 N spans several images, so c is per (image, k) and the producer indexes by token column), issue fence.proxy.async.shared::cta, then arrive on a per-stage g_ready mbarrier; the MMA warp waits g_ready instead of full. The producers run up to STAGES-2 stages ahead (they only need landed h, which the 6-deep TMA ring provides). Measure clk per stage again: the gating of r8 (~0.8 us per stage) must be gone. If a stage still exceeds 1.3x the two-MMA ideal, build the fallback: one accumulator, the half h tile scaled in place by s_b (sc_kernel form, h rounded twice), 32 KB stages of A 16 + h 16 at depth 6, and compare both forms on the stamps and the rows.
STEP 3 (measure and ship). Interleave parent vs candidate x3 in one container on the 6 tc rows (and confirm the 7 sc rows are untouched). run_tests 16/16 incl. portal-order re-runs. PRECISION LOG (mandatory, the roundings may change): fp64 reference, harness generators, torch.manual_seed(200), 10 rounds per row, max |err| vs own atol and beyond-own-atol count for all six tc rows and the shipped form; if the fallback form ships and any row exceeds 90 % of its atol, scale the A tile from fp32 W2 instead. Record: stage clk vs ideal for 1SM / pair / pair+smem-g, GEMM2 phase per row, GEMM1 post-accumulator per tile, interleaved deltas, smem and register budgets (512 threads, <= 128 regs, STACK 0). Success: GEMM2 per 64-k stage <= 1.3x the two-MMA ideal on the stamps at 8,768 and 32,768; GEMM1 post-accumulator per tile >= 40 % below the parent; interleaved x3 rows: 16,384 <= 46, 8,384 <= 30, 32,768 <= 57, 16,768 <= 39, 8,768 <= 29, 2,768 <= 24 us rented; 16/16 pass; precision log <= 90 % of own atol with 0 beyond on every tc row. Refuted if: Pairs alone cut the GEMM2 phase by < 2 us at 8,768 and 32,768 AND neither smem-g form brings the stage under 1.5x the ideal, so the rows end within 1.5 us of the parent on 4 or more of the 6 tc rows (then GEMM2 at 7x7 is bound by the per-unit fixed chain, TMEM alloc + first landing + drain + red, and the next lever is fewer units per row, not stage bytes). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) gsq / gw*gf arrays and every red.add target are zeroed or written inside this launch before first use, ordered by a grid sync. (b) If the cooperative+cluster launch is rejected and you fall back to a plain launch, check co-residency per shape (grid <= cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters x 2) every call. Any grid-barrier counter, generation word or flag must live in a module-level __device__ buffer (zero-initialised at module load) and be self-reset by the last arriver, never in the torch.empty workspace (uninitialised, not guaranteed to be the same memory or unchanged between calls). Experiment E3 (tests H40): tcgen05 kind::f16 GEMM1 in the single-tile fused kernel g_p1s for 8,320,32,32 and 4,96,56,56. STEP 0 (engine gate, ~10 B200 min, standalone probe). From the notebook recipe (H r8: idesc = (1<<4)|(1<<16)|(N>>3)<<17|(128>>4)<<24; A = 128x64 K-major SW128 box, SBO 1024, +32 B per k16; B = [channel][token] MN-major 64-token chunks, LBO 8192, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16; whole-warp TMA and MMA roles with elect.sync; tcgen05.alloc 512 columns then relinquish; tcgen05.ld 32x32b.x32 with the wait in one asm) build a one-CTA kernel that writes the B tile into smem with PLAIN st.shared in the canonical swizzled MN-major layout (the conv warps will write d16 this way, not via TMA), TMAs A from an fp16 W1' buffer, runs K = 128 (C=96 padded with zero channels) and K = 320 (5 k-blocks), N = 128, and compares the TMEM result bit-for-bit against torch fp16 matmul with fp32 accumulation (<= 1e-3 relative). Do not proceed until this passes on both K values; record the swizzle address function used by the writers.
STEP 1 (g_p1s port). Conv warps write the fp16 d tile directly into the SW128 MN-major layout from STEP 0 (drop the token permutation; the LN stats path is unchanged). Zero the pad channels 96..127 in the d tile at C=96 once per tile buffer. A operand: W1' from the K0 fp16 scratch via a TMA ring (C=320: 10 hidden blocks x 5 k-blocks of 16 KB, 4-stage ring replacing the bulk ring; C=96: 3 hidden blocks x 2 k-blocks = 96 KB, resident after one TMA load per CTA at kernel start, or ring-fed if smem is short). One MMA warp (warp-uniform role; only the issue inside elect.sync) walks hidden blocks: at 4,96 N=128 tokens x 3 hidden blocks = 384 TMEM columns in one shot; at 8,320 (64-token tiles) 10 blocks x 64 columns = 640 > 512, so two 256-column accumulator halves (blocks 0-3 / 4-7 / 8-9) ping-ponged with per-half commit barriers, so the epilogue of one half overlaps the MMA of the next. Epilogue on every non-conv warp: tcgen05.ld (TMEM lane = hidden row, columns = tokens: each thread holds one hidden row x 32 tokens, so the fp16 h store is one contiguous 64 B per thread per load, no transpose), LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + c1 with per-token (mu, rs) from smem and per-row (u, c1) in registers, A&S erfc GELU, per-(image,k) sumsq thread-local then red.add per tile as now, h16 store. Keep the double-buffered d tile so the conv of tile i+1 overlaps the MMA+epilogue of tile i. Budget: <= 128 regs at the current thread count, STACK 0, smem <= 227 KB (print both per instantiation). target_hardware [B200] only.
STEP 2 (measure). Stamps from the working warps at 8,320 and 4,96: conv end, first MMA issue, per-half MMA done, epilogue end, tile end; then per-launch harness_time (K0 / +P1 / +K3 / +G2) with the 6-try CUPTI retry wrapper. Interleave parent vs candidate x3 in one container at 4,96 and 8,320; confirm 64,96 / 32,128 are byte-identical paths (g_pass1 untouched) and unchanged within noise. run_tests 16/16 incl. portal-order re-runs.
STEP 3 (precision and report). PRECISION LOG for 4,96 and 8,320 (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds, max |err| vs own atol, beyond count); the accumulation order changes with the engine, so the log is mandatory. Record: engine gate result, stage clk vs the kind::f16 ideal, pass 1 per row, interleaved deltas, resources, and whether the same port is feasible for g_pass1 at 64,96 / 32,128 (smem for W1' ring + d double buffer at R=2 tiles, TMEM columns at N=224). Success: Pass 1 <= 30 us at 8,320 and <= 19 us at 4,96 on the stamps; interleaved x3 rows 8,320 <= 55 and 4,96 <= 33 us rented (r8: 67.2 / 37.0); 16/16 pass; precision log 0 beyond own atol on both rows; 64,96 / 32,128 unchanged. Refuted if: The engine gate passes but pass 1 at 8,320 improves by < 6 us (the mma.sync term was 16.2 us, so the epilogue or the A ring must then be the new binding term: report the stamp), or the port cannot fit the register/smem budget without dropping the double-buffered d tile.
